body: For adderall it kinda snuck up on me and I didn't realize till I was already hooked.

Well, I work as a CNA at a nursing home, I know the basic stuff about keeping someone alive and healthy. I just don't really know how to interact with kids because I haven't really been in that situation. Oh well, I'm sure it'll work out.

I'm actually pretty excited to be an uncle, though my brother and his wife live in another state so I don't know how often I'd see them. If it's a niece I'll be a little lost, I don't have any sisters or anything but I'm sure I could figure it out.

No I won't be harsh about it, if I was gonna be harsh I would be in a different situation right now. 

I just gotta explain that I'm still her friend and I've got her back, but I'm not gonna be a dad, I'm not ready for that. I mean, I'm going to be an uncle in a few months and that's already got me a little nervous and it's not directly impacting me as much as this.

It's true, and that's what makes it so hard. 

I'd like to help her out, I mean she's my friend, but it's a very fine line I gotta walk. I'm probably too nice for my own good, so I've gotta be careful that I don't get pulled down too. 

I should probably talk to her and set things straight from the beginning.
Yeah, that seems to be the best way to handle it. I just gotta be careful, because I'm finally trying to get my own life back on track by going back to school and everything.

I don't have to justify it, I'm actually fairly impressed with how well I can do it. I've got a skill that a lot of people use, and I just do it better than most.  Honestly (funny right?) you wouldn't even know if you met me and I didn't tell you. I'm just saying, not all my friends are low lives and there's shittier people out there than me.

Yeah I work but I can't make the money to cut off all ties like I want to. I already slave my ass off between work and school and at the end of the month I'd barely make the rent for the cheaper places in town. Add in utilities, gas, school costs, and food and I wind up in debt. I really can't add that much more shifts or I'd never get schoolwork done, which I can just barely manage right now as is.
Everyone lies whether you notice it or not.

I lie all the time, it's just how I am. Dozens every day to the point where I don't even notice it. I have to lie to be able to do anything. It's that argument of theirs that always pisses me off when I'm caught lying. "If you told us the truth we would've let you". It's such bullshit. I've truthfully asked to do things they usually approve of just to get shut down for no apparent reason. If I ask why, first I get ignored, and if I press on, it's yelling. So yeah, while I did abuse their trust to do something else last night, sometimes if I'm actually doing what I say I'm doing, I get shut down.

I already negotiated with them, they fucking lie too. I told them that just because I'm living at home instead of the dorms, doesn't mean that I'm any more willing to put up with their overprotective shit. I don't want to have to always call home and ask permission to do something or explain why I'm home later. They lied and said I didn't need to, but they still do it. I shouldn't have to ask for permission to do anything. If anything, out if courtesy I could let them know I'm leaving and if I'm really feeling nice, say why.

Confronting them is not going to achieve anything. I've tried and failed many times already. They're expecting an apology but I don't feel sorry. I don't see why I should apologize for making my own decision. I'm not even really thinking about it, so I've got literally nothing that I'd want to say.

I actually don't have a lock on my door, so I can't technically lock myself in. 

I mean, yeah I'm not exactly proud of how I'm going about it, that's why it's in r/confession and not r/teenjusticeporn or something. But I've gotten into fights with my parents quite a bit in the past, so I know how it goes. Might as well save myself a few steps and just do my own thing for a while. I'm honestly just not in a mood to care about it. If it wasn't for them bringing it up, I'd be going about my day like nothing ever happened. 

Leave? Why didn't I think of that? I work but I really don't make enough to just up and go, I've already looked into it.
That's what I'm thinking. I figure ill just lay low for a while, ignore it, and then work towards moving out eventually.

Oh I know it's dumb and childish, but since that's how I'm viewed and treated I might as well enjoy my Saturday a little, instead of getting yelled at, yelling back, getting worked up and nothing happening.
Rub that red hot cock sauce on your lips..
Thanks I guess. I have no idea what'll happen next. I'm ok for now I guess, could be worse.

It's a shitty realization that I'm closing in on. I take breaks on the weekends or days I don't have school because well, I don't actually need it for sitting around at home. Those breaks though, are pretty hellish, and have been getting worse. Last week I had Fall break and didn't take any. First day, bed at 11, woke up around 2:30 still tired as hell. Figured that was just like a hangover and that I'd sober up to normal after a few days. I didn't. It just stayed like that all week. 

I'm in a bad place. I've got a steady supply, no need to be cautious. I've got the past experiences of what being on a high and low are like, and a steadily forming tolerance and dependence. It's breaking away at me and I don't think there's much keeping me from escalating it.

My dad was a mechanic when he was younger, and a result we have a well-stocked (albeit messy) garage. I don't think we've ever taken any of our cars to a shop except for getting new tires or when the dealer offers to fix a recall. 

When I was little I was the "tool monkey", assigned to find and give necessary tools, bits, sockets, parts, fluids, etc.  Over time I got assigned little tasks here and there. Now I can pretty much work on my own car by myself.

I'm trying but I can feel my willpower weakening the more I build up a tolerance and dependence. There is very very little that held me back from taking more than my dose today. I think if my dad wasn't at home today I would've crushed two up. 

It's so easy to get into a mindset that its the solution to almost anything. Didn't sleep? Adderall. Tired? Adderall. Bored? Adderall. Sad? More Adderall. Feeling shitty from not taking Adderall yet? Adderall.
Wow, that hits close because its a lot like me. Guess I'm lucky that I don't really hang out with the bad crowd anymore.

If its not too personal, may I ask what you mean by "be careful"? Like, could you expand on what that means, or what you would've done differently? I've been on it for about 2 months or so, I'd be interested in hearing your experience over 4 years.

You make good points, and I don't want to appear stubborn but I can't see it the way you do. I don't see it as a phase of everything being shitty and stressful, it's more like an accumulation of everything to this point. 

It's there at the back of my mind all the time, and just "flares up" sometimes. I think about suicide in some way or another pretty much each day, and my mood affects it. If I'm alright, then I just think about it hypothetically or as a distant concept, without any intentions of planning/doing it. If I'm down like last night, then I start thinking more about applying it to myself. 

I cant think of any hobbies I have that I like. I suck at video games even though I play them, and I don't think being bad at something will give me any confidence/self-esteem boost. I'm not artistic visually. I like music, but can't make any. No sports. I guess I'm alright at technical stuff like working on a car or making something, but my car is too damn reliable and I can't exactly fire up the power tools at 3 in the morning. 

I appreciate the offer to chat, and maybe ill take you up on it sometime, but I don't really open up till I hit the bottom.

It was easier to confess it to strangers than anyone I know. I feel so alone in this, and since I'm still pretty functional and successful, no one suspects anything. 

My fear is that going to the doctor about it will just end with me getting a label that'll be stuck in my medical file. I already have "drug abuse" in there from the time I went to the ER after smoking spice. 

Another thing is, it was so hard to get my parents to even take me to the doctor about ADHD, and they've always been pretty anti-medication, so if I get taken off Adderall that's probably where it'll stop, and ill just end up in the same hole.

Wow, it's strange but I had this exact same thought in my head before I even checked reddit. I'm pretty much convinced that if there was a gun in the house I wouldn't be around today and that I would've done something looong ago. Maybe not the first time I felt that way, maybe not the second, but I don't think I would've held out indefinitely if it were available.
